findings.summary: __call__ passes argtuple (all args with array void pointers) instead of initargtuple (symbols only) as initargs to fast_call, which forwards to _initialize; the _init C function receives mismatched arguments
findings.failure_scenario: Any SDFG with an initialization function (self._init is not None) — _construct_args returns (newargs, initargs) where newargs contains c_void_p array pointers for every argument but initargs contains only ctypes-cast symbol args. The old code passed initargtuple correctly to _initialize; the new code passes argtuple, causing ctypes.ArgumentError when _init receives void pointers where it expects scalar types. The separate initialize() method at line 359 still correctly uses initargtuple, confirming this is a bug rather than an intentional API change.

findings.summary: v.parent.parent accessed without null guard on v.parent in deconstruct_interface_calls, risking AttributeError
findings.failure_scenario: If any value in alias_map (from alias_specs(ast)) has a None parent — for example, a node that was added to the map without being attached to the AST tree — isinstance(v, Interface_Stmt) is False and Python evaluates isinstance(v.parent.parent, Interface_Block), raising AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'parent'. While parsed AST nodes always have parent pointers, manual additions to alias_map elsewhere in the codebase could introduce parentless nodes.
